The lock-based version is preferred for its speed, as the lock-free version is 2 to 3 times slower due to group-level serial launches [S1].

The claim states that the lock-free version is slower due to 'group-level serial launches'. However, the evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states that the lock-free version involves dividing cubes into groups with no overlapping edges to allow 'lock-free parallel execution'. The evidence attributes the preference for the lock-based version to 'running time and memory' issues, specifically noting that the lock-free implementation causes '2 to 3 times additional memory consumption' due to memory leaks, not that it is slower due to serial launches. In fact, the lock-free method is described as running in parallel, whereas the performance penalty mentioned is related to memory usage and potential unexpected results, not serial execution overhead.
